messages:
jonas: Ran a focused perf pass on the fused-attn + TP scheduling branch this morning. Observed a recurring ~20-30% stall attributed to repeated small NCCL all-gather calls during decode when KV cache hits are high.

maria: Can you share the minimal perf slice? which kernel selection path did the runtime pick (flash vs aten fused fallback)?

jonas: Runtime picked flash-attn for the fused path, but Q/K/V all-gather is still being emitted as three separate NCCL ops from the TP layer. Perf snippet: ```GPU0: all_gather(Q) 0.09s, all_gather(K) 0.11s, all_gather(V) 0.08s -> GPU0 idle waiting for V scatter 0.22s```

kevin: Oof. small-message NCCL overhead + serialization. We've seen this pattern: separate small all-gathers lose comm/compute overlap. Did you try coalescing QKV into a single packed all-gather?

jonas: Yes — local patch that packs QKV into a single buffer before NCCL all-gather drops the comm time by ~3x on 8x A100 run. But it regresses memory peaks for long context because we allocate the packed buffer per microbatch.

ellie: @jonas can you check kvcache eviction/reshard? If scatter order differs across TP ranks we create implicit syncs. We had a bug where TP shard ordering reversed for the last microbatch which forced a full barrier.

jonas: Good call. I instrumented the shard order and saw occasional rank 3 doing scatter earlier, rank 5 later — ordering mismatch in our async scatter completion callbacks. That lines up with the spike.

maria: Two follow-ups: 1) Try coalesced all-gather with a reusable pre-allocated buffer (amortize the extra memory). 2) Add a short-circuit: if KV cache presents contiguous shards, use in-place allgather to avoid pack/unpack.

kevin: Also tweak batching heuristic: when sequence length variance across microbatches is low, favor aggregator that merges QKV. When variance high, prefer piecemeal to reduce peak memory.

jonas: Implemented a simple heuristic switch and benchmarked on the enwik8 style workload: coalesce wins for low variance latency (p95 down 18%), but high variance runs show 9% memory OOM risk.

ellie: We should also audit kernel selection fallbacks — I found cases where flash-attn chooses an index kernel that serializes across TP shards for specific head sizes. That interacts badly with our gather shape.

jonas: Right — on head_dim=64 and heads=16 the kernel fallback path dropped to aten fused which created extra CPU copies before NCCL. The profiler shows CPU->GPU memcopies at same timestamps as all-gather.

maria: Action items: 
- jonas: open repro + attach perf markers + flame graph (PR branch: `perf/fused-tp-gather`)
- kevin: prototype preallocated packed buffer + reclamation strategy (limit to N largest contexts)
- ellie: add assertion to check TP scatter order and a lightweight consistency marker to avoid accidental reorders
- infra: run nightly 8x and 4x regression suites with the heuristic on/off

jonas: Filed issue #4128 and pushed an initial trace in the branch. Link: https://git.redwood/reds/perf/4128 (internal). Small repro in `tests/perf/repro_kv_gather.py`.

sre-bot: Nightly job `perf-gather-8x` triggered for branch `perf/fused-tp-gather` — queued on pool `dedicated-8g`. ETA ~45m.

kevin: One more note — NCCL version differences change threshold where coalescing helps. We should matrix NCCL 2.12 vs 2.14; pack strategy tuning param should be safe to tweak remotely.

ellie: Great thread. If the prealloc approach looks good, we can enable it behind a feature flag and run canaries on Dedicated.

jonas: Will update the PR with perf numbers + memory numbers tomorrow. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:
